name: Lusitanian

ancestors.notes: Indo-European; exact subgroup disputed between Celtic-adjacent, Italic-adjacent, and pre-Celtic/pre-Italic western IE hypotheses (Wikipedia: Lusitanian language).

notes: Stub: no citable systematic grapheme-to-IPA inventory. Extinct Indo-European (Palaeohispanic) language of western Iberia (Lusitania), known from ~6 substantial inscriptions (c. 1st c. CE) plus theonyms and toponyms, written by bilingual speakers in the borrowed Latin alphabet -- Lusitanian had no native script. Sources describe individual sound-change arguments (c/g and t/d alternations suggesting lenition; likely intervocalic and post-r /β ɣ ð/ rather than Latin stop values) but not a complete, citable orthography-to-phoneme table, so a full `graphemes` map would overstate what is known; left empty rather than fabricated from Latin default values, which the Celtic/lenition evidence explicitly warns against. Classification (independent western IE branch vs. Celtic vs. Italic-linked) remains actively disputed, so only the safe IE parent is asserted.
